key_insight: TACO replaces dense optimizer state with a column-wise one-sparse update rule that preserves AdamW-like fine-tuning behavior while making optimizer memory nearly negligible.
engineering_relevance: This enables full-parameter LLM fine-tuning of much larger models on a single GPU by dramatically lowering persistent and peak memory without sacrificing accuracy or runtime.
method: Uses the exact steepest-descent direction under a dimension-normalized 1→1 operator norm.
For each matrix column, keeps only the sign of the largest-magnitude gradient entry.
Maintains a small set of low-precision gradient components per column instead of dense optimizer state.
evidence_signal: On OPT-13B, TACO reduced persistent optimizer state from 27.7 GB to 0.16 GB and peak training memory from 80.6 GB to 27.5 GB, with comparable accuracy and runtime; it also enabled 30–32B model fine-tuning on a single 80 GB H100.
watch_item: The one-sparse, column-wise geometry is tailored to matrix-shaped parameters, so careful implementation is needed to ensure stable behavior across all model layers and training setups.
paper_title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
